target: Restore automatic draining of frozen semantic-summary jobs while native capture produces rebuildable projection drift.
primary_semantics: Raw-integrity failures fail closed; rebuildable derived-view drift remains visible as attention but does not block source-hash-bound pending jobs.
invariants: Raw rollout files, append-only raw memory, persisted summaries, cloud replicas, and trusted-device records are never rewritten or deleted.
Every semantic ingest revalidates the frozen job source SHA-256 before commit.
A deep recovery audit is reused for at most one hour and explicit recovery debt always forces a fresh audit.
Repairable projection drift cannot be reported as healthy and cannot authorize creation of a new compensating summary job.
No manual dispatcher invocation may satisfy the automatic scheduled-drain effect gate.
allowed_changes: Separate raw-integrity blocking from rebuildable projection-repair reporting in semantic backfill.
Reuse recent deep-recovery evidence so the five-minute scheduler does not rebuild all derived views before every batch.
Add focused regression tests, runtime evidence, version metadata, and three-locale release notes.
prohibited_changes: Relax raw-source hash validation or raw-history integrity checks.
Rewrite, truncate, normalize, or delete raw history, persisted summaries, or pending job source assignments.
Treat repairable drift as healthy or run a broad full-release rehearsal for this narrow patch.
before_after_checks: Reproduce pending semantic debt remaining constant while supervisor reports repair-incomplete.
Run the focused semantic-backfill suite and preserve raw-integrity blocking coverage.
Install the candidate without manually dispatching a summary and require the next Windows scheduled tick to reduce pending debt.
